title: custom name of a customized built-in element is unreachable

labels.name: topic: custom elements
labels.description: Relates to custom elements (as defined in DOM and HTML)

body:
Use-case:
Framework working on DOM elements needs to process undefined custom elements only when defined.
For the regular __custom__ element it is simple:
```javascript
if (!element.matches(':defined') {
    customElements.whenDefined(element.localName).then(() => { ... do something ... });
}
```

But for __customized built-in__ element this is not possible, since `element.localName` is just a standard DOM element's name and there is no way right now to reach the extended name provided in `is` property:
```javascript
let element  = document.createElement('input', { is: 'custom-input' });
//   value of 'is' goes into internals and 'custom-input' becomes not reachable anymore
```

BTW, when the same element is being added as below, `is` handled as an attribute and __is__ reachable:
```javascript
someElement.innerHTML += '<input is="custom-input"/>';
someElement.firstChild.attributes.length === 1;                     // true
someElement.firstChild.getAttribute('is') === 'custom-input';       // true
```

Proposal:
- when customized built-in element is created __programmatively__, preserve `is` value as an attribute in a symmetric to `HTML`ish syntax. As proposed by someone (see refs below) it should probably be readonly IDL attribute
- unify behavior of `is` to be the same either provided from `createElement` JS API or coming from HTML's attribute


Appendix:
- relevant SO thread: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39196503/how-to-wait-for-custom-element-reference-to-be-upgraded/52420195#52420195
- relevant Chromium issue: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=886991&can=2&start=0&num=100&q=&colspec=ID%20Pri%20M%20Stars%20ReleaseBlock%20Component%20Status%20Owner%20Summary%20OS%20Modified&groupby=&sort=
